leaves.analysis: The production hierarchy has 21 authored ordinary subsystems and one actually linked Debouncer definition (deduplicated), all with identifiable single responsibilities. The five top roles separate fault aggregation, operating mode, battery-state accounting, cell-voltage monitoring and temperature monitoring. Four second-level threshold groups have 18 direct blocks each; twelve third-level debounce wrappers have seven each. Tool-generated Stateflow representation is excluded. Generic wrapper names remain a naming weakness and repeated wrapper logic a reuse weakness; neither alone proves unclear hierarchical responsibilities.

leaves.analysis: 1 retained: four max/min cell-voltage/module-temperature fault groups separately implement the same 19-block, three-severity threshold/debounce/precedence topology; their twelve seven-block wrappers are also identical in topology. Threshold values, > versus < direction, V versus temperature units and separate calibrated debounce times are legitimate differences that can be explicit parameters of one definition. Each shared-definition instance can retain independent state; no source requirement for an independently qualified fork was found. Twelve actual BMSLib/Debouncer links are positive reuse evidence, but do not remove the duplicated upper monitoring logic. Thus 0 ignores real reuse, while 2 requires the absence of this avoidable duplicate logic. The previous SID 120 was a wrapper, not the linked block; direct negative group anchors and actual SID 126 link now distinguish these facts.

leaves.analysis: The former tier 3 is contradicted by Stateflow SOC and voltage-ratio guards, repeated hard-coded initial capacities/cell counts/voltages and independent execution timing. Independent census finds 43 centralized business quantities, six additional noncentralized quantities and hard-coded copies of five centralized quantities. Most business quantities are therefore centralized; tier 1 literally requiring a scattered majority is also not established. Tier 0 is not supported. This contract gap is unresolved: no integer is imputed pending an explicit tier-1 interpretation.
